newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australian bonds hugging near unchanged levels.
newsitem.headline: Australian bonds hugging near unchanged levels.

text.p: *Australian bond futures were hugging close to Thursday's levels as the market patiently awaited next week's RBA board and FOMC meetings, and after finding support on downside moves.
Australian bond futures were hugging close to Thursday's levels as the market patiently awaited next week's Reserve Bank board and Federal Open Market Committee meetings.

Several moves to the downside during the morning session found support on the view that the market has more than compensated for its over bullishness on a rate cut next week after the sell-off in the past two sessions.
September bill futures have now got just a 25 basis point easing fully priced in rather than nearer the 50 basis point level seen at the start of the week.
May motor registrations fell 0.7 percent after a revised 6.1 percent drop in April and against median expecations for a 1.5 percent rise.
While not usually a market mover it added to the argument for the need for a policy easing to push growth along and was a further sign the consumer confidence is far from blooming.

Meanwhile, U.S. Treasuries were under further pressure in Tokyo trading after about of profit-taking in New York, triggered by a drop in the weekly jobless claims report on Thursday and after this week's strong data for consumer confidence and home sales.

Yield differentials tightened sharply to Canada after the Bank of Canada's surprise 25 basis points tightening. Conversely spreads widened to New Zealand after the RBNZ endorsed a larger than expected loosening in monetary conditions in its Monetary Policy Statement.
